case_title: Bhaiyamiyan @ Jardar Khan & Anr. v. State of Madhya Pradesh
evidence_type: Victim testimony, parents' testimony, medical evidence (doctor examined about 24 hours after the incident), petticoat seized and sent for examination
trial_court_outcome: Accused acquitted after cumulative assessment of prosecution evidence
high_court_outcome: State's appeal against acquittal allowed; accused convicted under s.376(2)(g) IPC and sentenced to 10 years RI and fine of Rs.25,000 (default two years RI)
neutral_facts: On the morning of 30 August 1984, the victim went out to relieve herself. While returning home she was intercepted by the accused, taken to a nearby field and raped. The accused threatened her with consequences if she disclosed the incident. She returned home and told her parents, who accompanied her to the police outpost at Pathriya, where no police official was present. The next day, around 12:15 p.m., she lodged a report at Sironj Police Station, about 22 km from the place of incident, although Unarasital police station was only 7 km away. At her insistence, and after declining examination at Sironj, she was medically examined at a hospital at Vasoda, about 55 km away. The examining doctor, who examined her about 24 hours after the incident, found no injury on the genitalia and deposed that the tear in the hymen was old, so there was no evidence of rape. The victim stated that her vagina had been stitched, but the doctor found no stitches. The investigation was conducted by Unarasital police, who seized the victim's petticoat and sent it for examination. The parents' account was based on what the victim had told them.
physical_harm: No injury found on the victim's genitalia on medical examination; tear in hymen found to be old
key_evidence_accepted: Medical report showing no genital injury and doctor's evidence that there was no evidence of rape (old hymen tear); court relied on the delay and unexplained choice of medical examination venue
witness_credibility: Court found the explanation for the delay in lodging the FIR difficult to believe and the prosecution unable to explain why the victim insisted on examination at Vasoda; the doctor's evidence was relied on
bail_history: Appellants on bail at the Supreme Court stage; bail bonds discharged on acquittal
trial_duration: offence: 30 August 1984; trial judgment: 6 January 1992; High Court: 22.4.2004; Supreme Court: 3 May 2011
legal_representation: Accused: Ashok Mathur; State: Vibha Dattaa Makhija
investigation_status: FIR lodged about 60 hours after incident at Sironj Police Station; investigation conducted by Unarasital police; accused charged under s.376(2)(g) IPC
procedural_irregularity: Delay of about 60 hours in lodging FIR and lodging it at a station about 22 km away though a closer station existed; victim declined examination at Sironj and insisted on examination at Vasoda, 55 km away, unexplained
appeal_history: Trial court: acquitted. High Court: State's appeal allowed, conviction under s.376(2)(g) IPC with 10 years RI and fine. Supreme Court: appeal allowed, conviction set aside, accused acquitted
legal_principle_applied: In an appeal against acquittal, the High Court's interference is circumscribed; if the trial court's view was possible on the evidence, the appellate court should not interfere merely because it might have taken a different view
other_sentence_order: Bail bonds of the appellants discharged
